c183.title: Empires of the East
c183.story: On Tuesday, Taras had a history lesson about great empires of the East. First, the teacher showed a picture of a [[sultan]] in his huge palace. The women of his family lived in a separate part called the [[harem]]. A loyal [[eunuch]] guarded its doors day and night. Far from the palace, a [[pasha]] ruled a busy port city for the sultan. Next, the class read about a wise [[caliph]] who loved books and science. His [[caliphate]] was bigger than many countries today. Then came a powerful [[khan]] and his army of horse riders. His people were [[nomads|nomad]] who moved their tents across the wide [[steppe]]. Taras laughed at a drawing of a hairy [[yak]] carrying their bags. Finally, a rich maharaja signed an [[edict]] that opened free schools for poor children. For homework, Taras drew a map of all four empires and got the best mark.

c184.title: Warriors of the Past
c184.story: Max loves military history, so he spent all Saturday with a thick book. First, he read about a brave [[gladiator]] who fought in a huge arena. A Roman [[centurion]] led a hundred men from his [[legion]] across the hills. In the next chapter, a [[paladin]] defended a small [[fort]] against a big army. When the fort fell, he ran up to the stone [[citadel]] on the hill. Max loved the part where a [[musketeer]] fought a [[duel]] at dawn. Then he read about a [[samurai]] with two swords who served the [[shogun]]. The last story was about a port town, the final [[bastion]] against an enemy [[armada]]. With a clever [[maneuver]], its few small ships hid behind an island and won. In the evening, Max told Anna every story, and she fell asleep on the sofa.

c187.title: Grandma's Church
c187.story: At Easter, Anna went to church with Grandma early in the morning. The [[pastor]] spoke about the [[archangel]] Michael and the coming of the [[messiah]]. After the service, they had tea with Grandma's friend Rosa, a [[Catholic]] from Lviv. Rosa explained that in [[Catholicism]], baptism and marriage are each a [[sacrament]]. She showed them a small [[crucifix]] from her mother. She also explained which old books are part of the Bible's [[canon]]. Her cousin once saw a [[cardinal]] in a red robe at a [[synod]] in Rome. Grandma remembered her own father, who met a kind [[padre]] in the army. The man prayed with the soldiers before every hard day. Later, Rosa invited them to a monastery where an old [[abbot]] makes honey. Anna said yes at once, because she loves honey more than anything. On the way home, she carried Grandma's heavy bag, and Grandma called her a real [[angel]].

c188.title: An Evening of Many Faiths
c188.story: Anna's college held an evening of many faiths in the big hall. First, a [[Protestant]] student talked about her church choir. A [[Baptist]] from a small town shared his family's Sunday traditions. A friendly [[Mormon]] spoke about helping neighbors, and an old [[Quaker|quaker]] talked about silence and peace. Then a Jewish [[cantor]] sang a beautiful old song. Next, an [[imam]] and another [[cleric]] came to the stage. The second man was a [[mullah]], and together they explained the basics of [[Islam]]. They told the students about fasting during [[Ramadan]] and sharing food with the poor. Pork and alcohol, they said, are [[haram]] for many Muslims. The imam explained that [[jihad]] means struggle, often to be a better person. He added that an [[Islamist]] has political goals, which is different from simply being Muslim. At the end, everyone ate cookies together, and Max ate the most.

c191.title: Grandma's Folk Tales
c191.story: On a snowy evening, Grandma told Anna and Max old tales from world [[folklore]]. First came a hungry [[ghoul]] who lived in an old cemetery. Then a [[banshee]] cried in the night, and a tiny [[leprechaun]] hid his gold. Max liked the story of a [[yeti]] who helped lost climbers in the mountains. Anna loved the [[phoenix]] that rose again from its own ashes. A village [[healer]] gave a sick boy a [[talisman]] for luck and an [[amulet]] against illness. A [[druid]] in the forest made a magic [[elixir]] from herbs. Far away, a [[shaman]] danced around a tall [[totem]] to call the rain. The people of one tribe prayed to a golden [[idol]] in a cave. A [[charlatan]] tried to sell the villagers fake magic, but nobody bought it. "And where did your old ring come from?" Max asked Grandma. Grandma just smiled, and the ring stayed an [[enigma]].
